findings.diagnosis: The prompt routinely treats a pre-verbal fragment as self-contained and allows cuts immediately before a clause’s main finite verb or copula, leaving the preceding piece without its predicate and producing high-contradiction/low-cohesion outputs.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_89','en_us_378','en_us_574','en_us_360','en_us_399','en_us_381','en_us_1144','en_us_577'] — each contains a kept marker that falls immediately before the clause's main finite verb or copula so the left-side fragment lacks its predicate or essential verbal complement.
findings.type_predicate: a marker that immediately precedes a finite verb or copula which serves as the main predicate of the clause

edit.text: Do not cut immediately before a clause’s main finite verb or copula; keep the verb (and any auxiliary) together with its subject and essential complements.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt allows cuts that split a noun head from an essential post‑nominal modifier (appositive, restrictive 'which/that' clause, prepositional complement, title or multiword name), underestimating the cohesion loss when the modifier defines or identifies the noun.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_1355','en_us_998','en_us_119','en_us_1215'] — each case has a kept marker placed between a noun head and an immediately following essential post‑nominal modifier (relative clause, appositive, title or multiword name) that the offline target preserves.
findings.type_predicate: a marker that falls between a noun (head) and an immediately following post‑nominal modifier that identifies, restricts, or names that noun (appositive/which‑clause/prepositional complement/title/multiword name)
